content.title: About
content.content: Fruit pancakes are thin, pan‑fried cakes made from a batter of flour, eggs, milk, and a touch of sugar, topped or folded with fresh or canned fruit. They have a delicate texture, a mildly sweet aroma, and a juicy fruit filling.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pancakes are a traditional staple in Russia and Eastern Europe, and fruit‑filled versions have become popular worldwide for their taste and nutrition.
More than 30 fruit varieties are commonly used: strawberry, banana, blueberry, raspberry, kiwi, and others.
Pancakes can be served sweet or savory; fruit pancakes are usually accompanied by sour cream, yogurt, or honey.
Thin pancakes cook in 1–2 minutes per side, making them a quick breakfast option.

items.title: Rich in vitamins
items.content: Fruits in the filling provide vitamin C, vitamin A, and folate, supporting immunity and vision.

items.title: Source of fiber
items.content: Fruit and whole‑grain flour add dietary fiber that promotes healthy digestion.

items.title: Low glycemic impact
items.content: Thin whole‑grain pancakes cause a slower rise in blood sugar compared with regular white‑flour pancakes.

items.title: Energy boost
items.content: The combination of carbohydrates from the batter and natural fruit sugars quickly replenishes energy stores.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Berries such as blueberries and raspberries are high in antioxidants that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Fruit allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to certain fruits like strawberries or kiwi.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Fruit pancakes can contain a lot of natural sugar; people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Heat‑related compounds
items.content: Over‑cooking pancakes may produce acrylamide, a potentially harmful compound.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve fruit pancakes hot, rolled or folded, drizzled with honey, yogurt, maple syrup, or dusted with powdered sugar. They make a great breakfast or light dessert.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked pancakes in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. Freeze in a single layer separated by parchment if you need longer storage (up to 2 months). Reheat gently with a splash of water to prevent drying out.
